_why: The old-to-new chapter map. Feature 045, FR-007 and FR-014.
ONE RECORD, THREE CONSUMERS: the published mapping page, the 48 redirects in
next.config.ts, and the chapter registry in relay-tutorial/lib/tutorial.ts that the
sitemap and six components read. The plan said two consumers until analysis counted
them. A hand-maintained list cannot be checked, and neither can a hand-maintained
count of who reads it.
TWENTY-FOUR BECOMES TWENTY-FIVE. One chapter splits: the error registry is needed by
every chapter that adds a refusal, and ten chapters currently add codes to a registry
the reader does not meet until chapter fourteen. The outsider is the SRS Phase 2 exit
criterion and nothing may follow it.
FOUR CHAPTERS KEEP THEIR NUMBER AND CHANGE MEANING — 3.13, 3.14, 3.15 and 3.16 all
exist before and after and name different chapters. That is the sharpest argument for
the named-reference rule: an ordinal that survives a reorder pointing at different
content is worse than one that breaks.
THE GUARD'S TABLE ARRAY GROWS PER CHAPTER, AND NO CHAPTER NAMES A COUNT.
New 8's section 'Nine guarded tables, not five' was an AUDIT of chapters 3.10 and
3.11 — 'neither added them here' — and both now land at 23 and 24. A chapter that
audits earlier chapters cannot be reordered ahead of them, and no instrument in
either repository reads that sentence. The section is deleted rather than moved:
each chapter adds its own table to the array, plants its bait, and drives it in
guard.itest.ts. That also disposes of sentinel.sql's running count ('TEN AS OF
CHAPTER 3.16'), a number the reorder scrambles and nothing checks.
`was_url` IS THE REDIRECT'S SOURCE, and it is recorded here because a redirect needs the
OLD slug and this map only ever carried the new one. Twenty-four of the twenty-six have
one; the two without are the halves the split created, which never had a URL to redirect.
Matched BY SLUG rather than by number: old 12 and old 14 each split, and the old slug is
what says which new chapter inherits the address — `milestone-the-isolation-gauntlet` went
to new 25, not to new 4. That is why T038 asks for 48 redirects across 26 chapters.

TITLES COME FROM THE PAGES, NOT FROM THE PLAN. Five of the twenty-six disagreed with their page's own `metadata.title` — four were shortened labels and chapter 6's was a re-narration the page never adopted ('JetStream, and the grammar a subject needs' against the published 'JetStream and the first consumer', which is still what the chapter builds). The page is the artifact a reader sees, so the page wins, and `check-movements.py` asserts map, plan table and page agree.

why: FORCED BY A DEPENDENCY, NOT CHOSEN FOR BALANCE. The gauntlet creates eight files
and 25 chapter-edits land on them; moving it to the end of movement VIII put every
one of those edits before the file existed, and `ours` came back 0 lines on all
eight. A merge cannot resolve that — taking `theirs` only relocates the conflict to
the creator's own add/add. The harness must precede its editors and the verdict
belongs at the end, so the chapter divides at the question that opens the
THE HALVES FENCE DISJOINT PATHS, which is what makes the division mechanical: the
early half builds the gauntlet and its production code, the late half adds unit
tests OF the instruments. `catalogue.ts` early and `catalogue.test.ts` late;
`targets.ts` early and `targets.test.ts` late. No path appears in both.

reassignments._why: NOT A SPLIT, AND CHECK-MAP WAS RIGHT TO REFUSE IT AS ONE. A split divides a chapter's PROSE at a heading and gives each half its own page. Old 3.10's page is ten sections and every one of them is about quotas — 'The query we did not write' through 'What it costs'. There is no harness section to move, because nobody ever wrote one.
reassignments.finding: FEATURE 030 SHIPPED INSIDE OLD 3.10'S SPAN WITHOUT A CHAPTER. Sixteen commits built packages/test-harness and the global-operation guard; old 3.10's prose does not mention them. That is why new 8 (old 3.13) AUDITS the guard rather than building it — 'It watched five tables. Chapters 3.10 and 3.11 added four more … and neither added them here.' Three chapters excerpt the harness's files and none of them builds it. The reorder is what surfaced this: in the published order the audit had its antecedents in front of it and read fine.
reassignments.consequence: New 8 gains the sections nobody wrote, and loses the audit. Its prose now builds the harness — the package, the trigger, the two kinds of bait, the exemption that returns NEW on an UPDATE — and the five-to-nine retrofit story is gone, because the array grows per chapter now.
